meaning:
νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ
(dimin. of νεανίας) [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר, also for בָּחוּר, etc. ;]
a young man, youth: Mat.19:20, 22, Mrk.14:51 16:5, Luk.7:14, Act.2:17" (LXX) Act.23:18, 22, 1Jn.2:13-14; of an attendant (cf. Gen.14:24, al.) : Act.5:10.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”
A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,
He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
‘It will be in the last days, says God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see…
I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you…
